newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron's Arabs prepare hero's welcome for Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Hebron's Arabs prepare hero's welcome for Arafat.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Hebron on Sunday to lay claim to most of the city, the prize of months of bitter negotiations with Israel's right-wing leader Benjamin Netanyahu.
Crowds surged forward as Arafat's helicopter landed at the hilltop military governor's office from where Israel ran its 30-year-long occupation until last Friday.
Security guards cancelled an honour-guard review because of the crush and whisked Arafat into a car.

About 25,000 Hebronites pressed around the building for a glimpse of the leader who is now in control of seven West Bank towns and Gaza under an interim self-rule agreement. He shook hands with well-wishers from inside an open top car on his way into the building, known locally as al-Amara.
In his speech to the cheering crowd, Arafat said Sheikh Ahmed Yassin, the blind spiritual leader of the militant Islamic group Hamas, would be released soon from an Israeli jail.

"I tell the shabiba (activists) that your brother Sheikh Ahmed Yassin will be released soon," Arafat said, adding that the Jewish state would also free Palestinian women prisoners "within a few days".
The release of prisoners, especially the wheelchair-bound Yassin, would shore up Arafat's support on the Palestinian street, including in Hebron, a stronghold of Moslem militant activism.

The agreement on Hebron, reached after much diplomatic arm-twisting by the United States, has revived hopes that Arafat and Prime Minister Netanyahu can see the wider self-rule accord through to a final settlement of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in 1999.
Palestinians had decorated the 80 percent of Hebron under their control with Palestinian flags and posters for the man they call "Abu Amr".
Arafat's stubbled jowls smiled down from a mural erected on a hill overlooking the enclaves where some 400 armed Jewish settlers live and study in the heart of the town of 100,000 Palestinians.
They call Arafat a murderer and see the agreement he signed with Netanyahu as a betrayal of their biblical right to all of the West Bank.
Both Arab and Jew fear violence from each other in Hebron where some 2,000 Israeli soldiers will stay to protect the settlers.
"If these Jewish settlers in Hebron who have been provocative to Palestinans here do not make problems there will be no problems in Hebron," said West Bank Palestinian security chief Jibril Rajoub.
He is in charge of the 400 uniformed police and an undisclosed number of plainclothes police who deployed in Hebron after the last Israeli soldiers slipped away at dawn on Friday.

But Palestinian security sources said more than the 400 police stipulated under the deal were in the city along with several hundred plainclothes police, with Israel's tacit approval. The sources said Rajoub would move his headquarters to Hebron from Jericho.

Rajoub, whose forces have been accused of human rights violations by civil rights groups, told Reuters: "We will punish any Palestinian who violates the law and any policeman who maltreats Palestinians will also be punished."
Colonel Gadi, Israel's brigade commander in Hebron whose last name cannot be published, said animosity could not be easily overcome.
"Hebron has very tough, bad memories that go back a long way. I think it will take a long time to create different ways of thought," he told Israel Radio.
In February 1994, settler Baruch Goldstein from the nearby Kiryat Arba settlement massacred 29 Arabs kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque before survivors beat him to death.
In 1929 Arab rioters opposed to rising Jewish immigration killed 67 Jews.
